evidence.note: First wave of parity failures (EDA, BIF roundtrip, isolated_nodes): agent inspects failing-test detail, then edits link.rs and xml.rs and re-runs — local corrections tied to observed diffs, showing responsiveness but early on more like targeted tweaks.

Display-options and color diffs: rather than hardcode, agent views displayOptions goldens then traces the Java reference (AnnotColorSource, color map function, ColorGenerator) and refactors default.rs/xml.rs — treating the diff as a wrong model and fixing the general rule.
Persistent align_perfect diff prompts reading NetworkAlignmentEdgeLayout.java and NetworkAlignmentLayout to recover the real layout rule rather than fudging output.

Stubborn align_partial diff: agent returns to Java source (bfsNodeGroupLayout, nodeGroupAnnots, nodeGroupOrder constant) to find the real ordering/grouping rule and edits layout/groups/merge accordingly — strong root-cause tracing, though the many alternating edits and repeated runners.rs edits suggest some iterative patching/thrash.
triangle_fixed color diff: agent checks color_index assignment logic and fixes the general color-index rule in default.rs rather than special-casing the case.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly treats a stubborn byte-diff as a signal that its model of Java behavior is wrong, tracing back to specific reference files and constants (comparators, color sources, layout constants) and refactoring the general logic — squarely the level-8 behavior. It falls short of a clean 8-10 because early fixes are more local-tweak (level 3-5) and the align_partial arc shows considerable alternating edits and repeated test-runner edits that read as iterative patching, and the index-only trajectory hides the prose that would confirm systematic class-vs-one-off discipline. That places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8.
